History of Present Illness:
Mr. ___ is a ___ M with connective tissue disorder resulting 
in polychondritis developing acute respiratory failure s/p 
tracheostomy and multiple endobronchial dilations now with 
recurrence of LMS and BI stenosis. 

He was admitted early ___ with dyspnea and hypoxemia (in 
the setting of patient having stopped prednisone) then 
developing respiratory arrest after difficult intubation for 
attempted procedure to dilate airways. He had developed complete 
collapse of left mainstem bronchus as well as bronchus 
intermedius and tracheal stenosis. He was again admitted on 
___ for placement of T tube which was unsuccessful. 

He underwent ENT procedure today with KTP laser to subglottic 
area in attempts to debulk, however was found to have stenosis 
of left mainstem and bronchus intermedius. He was not having any 
worsening shortness of breath, significant cough or mucus 
production. Notes improved dryness in airway after addition of 
trach humidification adapter. He then went for procedure by IP 
and head/neck surgery where he was noted to have recurrent 
severe airway stenosis with trach in place. He underwent 
dilation of multiple upper airways. He tolerated the procedure 
well and was on supplemental O2 in PACU while recovering from 
anesthesia.
 
On the floor,  patient reports he is feeling very well and 
denies chest pain, SOB, fevers, chills, joint pain, nausea. He 
is in no acute distress and is on supplemental oxygen with 
humidified air. He typically uses supplemental oxygen at home.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ M with connective tissue disorder resulting 
in polychondritis developing acute respiratory failure s/p 
tracheostomy and multiple endobronchial dilations now with 
recurrence of LMS and BI stenosis s/p dilatation by IP on ___. 


ACUTE ISSUES:
# Acute on Chronic Respiratory Failure - Left mainstem and 
bronchus intermedius stenosis due to complications of his 
undefined connective tissue disorder. He is now s/p dilation of 
multiple upper airways by IP and ENT. His trach was exchanged by 
ENT on ___ who noticed severe airway stenosis requiring 
dilation by IP the same day. He was admitted to medicine after 
the procedure. His home dose of prednisone was increased to 60mg 
for 2 days. A baseline CXR was unremarkable, and he was 
continued on a trach collar with humidified air to keep oxygen 
saturations above 95%. Rheumatology evaluated him and 
recommended prednisone 60mg x 2 days, 50 mg x 2 days, 40 mg x 2 
days and then resuming his home dose of 30 mg. Additionally, 
they will help to arrange initiation of Enbrel after discharge.

# Polychondritis: Patient has a hx of non-well-defined genetic 
disorder with short stature, precocious puberty, contractures 
and pericarditis with noninflammatory fluid with recurrent 
stenosis in his tracheobronchial trees and multiple 
interventions and dilatation with inflammatory findings on his 
transbronchial biopsy suggestive of relapsing polychondritis. He 
was followed by rheumatology outpatient. Rheumatology was 
consulted as above. Bactrim was also started during this 
admission for infection prophylaxis as patient has been taking 
chronic 30mg prednisone and will be discharged on a steroid 
taper as above. 

# Leukocytosis - 19 on ___ after increasing prednisone from 
30mg to 60mg. Likely from steroid dose increase or from 
procedure the day prior as differential showed 92% PMNs. He 
showed no signs of infection, and has been afebrile. CXR was 
negative. 

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# GERD - continued famotidine 20mg
# Constipation - continued lactulose prn

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
- Patient has not been taking Bactrim SS tablet. Because he has 
been on chronic 30mg prednisone, then increased to 60mg with 
taper as above.
- Patient has follow-up with rheumatology on ___. 
- Patient has ENT follow-up on ___.
- Patient will need pulmonology follow-up in about 2 weeks. He 
will be contacted with an appointment and should call ___ if he does not hear back.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___, 

It was a pleasure to participate in your care at ___. You were 
admitted for an ENT procedure and were discovered to have airway 
closing that required dilation abain by our interventional 
pulmonologists. You tolerated the procedures well. You were also 
evaluated by our rheumatologists, who recommended that you taper 
down the 60mg prednisone we started you on. 

You should also call their nurse, ___, at 
___ to set up the Enbrel delivery. You took 60mg 
prednisone for 2 days while you were here. You should take 50mg 
on ___ and 40mg on ___. After that, you should 
return to taking your home dose of 30mg daily. 

You should continue to use the humidified air to thin your 
secretions at home while your tracheostomy is in place. 

We wish you all the best!
Your ___ team
